notes: The published water rate is per one hundred cubic feet. The conversion to cubic metres is declared in the component and performed by the engine, never silently.
The wastewater charge is defined as a percentage of the water charge, so it is stored as a percentage over a declared base rather than as a rate per volume.
The minimum metered charge of USD 0.49 per day per meter is not binding at this volume: it would total about USD 178.85 a year against an actual water charge of about USD 340.

reference_connection.designation: The Rate Schedule sets one metered rate per 100 cubic feet with no connection-size parameter, and the minimum charge is per day rather than per meter size — confirmed, not inferred, on 17 August 2026.

component_states.resolution: Resolved 17 August 2026. The Water Board sets a minimum charge for meter-billed customers of USD 0.49 per day for water service, plus wastewater at 159% of water charges, frozen since FY2017. It is not a meter-size charge — the hypothesis this record was withheld on was wrong about its form and right that something existed. Modelled as a floor on the bill rather than a component of it, and not applicable at the reference volume where usage exceeds it.

minimum_charge.rate_display: USD 0.49 per day minimum for meter-billed customers, with wastewater at 159% of water charges
minimum_charge.note: Frozen at USD 0.49 a day since FY2017 and maintained for FY2027. Not a meter-size charge, which was the hypothesis this record was withheld on. It does not bind at the reference volume: usage of USD 340.08 a year exceeds the floor of USD 178.97. It binds below about 7.9 m3 a month, which is why the price curve is not flat at 5 m3 although the rate never changes.

no_reconciliation_available.detail: The Board publishes a rate schedule and DEP publishes typical annual bills at 70,000 gallons a year, which is about 22 m3 a month and not the reference volume. Neither computes 15 m3. The tariff is deterministic: one rate per 100 cubic feet, wastewater at 159% of water charges, and a minimum that does not bind at this volume.
no_reconciliation_available.candidate: DEP's typical-bill figure of about USD 1,297 a year at 70,000 gallons could be reconciled against once the multi-family and service-line elements it may include are separated. Not attempted.

validation_note: Source verified and calculation verified. No reconciliation at the reference volume exists to perform.

continuity.note: The Water Board's adopted FY2027 rate schedule as captured 14 August 2026. The Board adopts rates annually, so this record will close with an effective_to when the FY2028 schedule is captured rather than remaining open-ended indefinitely.
